It sounds when the head is struck with a felt mallet, a stick or a pedal beater, and a heavy stroke gives a low note; a beginner can first practise a steady beat, such as beats one and three in 4/4, then learn the roll and double mallets.
大鼓常見於管絃樂團、合奏團與音樂會管樂團，也作為爵士鼓組中的踏板大鼓、軍樂隊與步: The bass drum is common in orchestras, in wind ensembles and in concert bands, and also as the pedal bass drum of the jazz kit and as the tuned bass drum of the military band and the marching band. In marches it marks the tempo; in rock and jazz it often plays beats one and three of each bar, and in jazz it can also take a melodic part. In electronic music it appears in American footwork and in African gqom. Prokofiev used the bass drum in place of the timpani in orchestral suites such as The Love for Three Oranges, Lieutenant Kijé and Romeo and Juliet; Gabriel Prokofiev has even written a bass drum concerto.

The shell was originally of wood, and lighter synthetic-fibre materials are now used too. The tuning gear usually adjusts the head tension with threaded rods or rope. Its sound is deeper than other drums; the length of the ring depends on size, head tension and the angle at which it is mounted, but size alone does not decide the volume. The player controls the striking position and force with a felt mallet, a stick, a pedal beater, two mallets or the hand, and a single stroke, a roll or a heavy stroke change the thickness and the sense of sustain. Unlike the timpani, the bass drum usually substitutes a low-frequency impact for a definite pitch; unlike the jazz pedal bass drum, the orchestral bass drum rings longer, while the jazz type is more compact.

The bass drum (Italian: gran cassa) belongs to the membranophones, Hornbostel–Sachs 211.212.1. The shell is mostly cylindrical, usually wider in diameter than it is deep, with heads at both ends of cow hide or plastic, tuned by threaded rods or rope. It is struck with a mallet, a pedal beater or the hand, giving a deep sound that may or may not have a definite pitch. It is common in the orchestra, the drum kit, the military band, the marching band and the drum and bugle corps: the orchestral drum rests on a stand, the kit drum is controlled by a pedal, and the marching drum is carried on a harness.
最早已知前身是土耳其 davul，雙面圓柱鼓，音色深沉，18世紀奧斯曼軍樂隊使用: Its earliest known predecessor is the Turkish davul, a double-headed cylindrical drum with a deep sound, used in Ottoman military bands in the eighteenth century and also in folk dance. The idea reached Africa, where it developed into the long drum hollowed from a tree trunk, used mainly in religion; it then came to Europe, where the single-headed gong drum appeared in nineteenth-century Britain; its definite pitch made it hard to fit the orchestra, and it was improved into the double-headed orchestral bass drum. In 1909 William Ludwig made the bass drum pedal, in the 1960s rock drummers began to use several bass drums, and in the twentieth century the Russian composer Prokofiev also used the bass drum in place of the timpani; his grandson Gabriel Prokofiev wrote the first bass drum concerto.
